title: Entergy New Orleans completes 200 miles of tree trimming to strengthen grid reliability
summary: Entergy New Orleans is investing in a stronger, more resilient electric grid while protecting the city’s unique tree canopy. As part of these efforts, we completed 200 miles of tree trimming across New Orleans to reduce outages, enhance public safety and strengthen our electrical infrastructure. Source

title: GLE and Silex announce final EIS for Paducah enrichment facility
summary: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission has released a final environmental impact statement for Global Laser Enrichment’s proposed Paducah Laser Enrichment Facility (PLEF) near Paducah, Ky. GLE and Silex Systems—the Australian firm that holds 51 percent ownership of GLE and that developed the enrichment technology to be used at the PLEF—announced that the EIS supports the issuance of a license to begin construction work on the facility. GLE completed its application for the license in July 2025.

title: European GenAI Platform Now Runs In Production Across All Swiss Nuclear Power Plants
summary: GRAYOAK Nuclear, a European provider of generative AI for the nuclear sector, has confirmed that its platform is now in active use at every Swiss nuclear power plant, developed in close partnership with operator Axpo. Twelve months after go-live, the system – known internally as “Lise” – processes more than 1,800 messages per day and has indexed over 550,000 documents spanning more than 50 years of operational history, with an 80% active-user rate among staff

title: Legacy cleanup supports modernization and economic development in Oak Ridge
summary: Cleanup across the Department of Energy’s Oak Ridge Reservation is bringing economic opportunities to the region while also making land available for continuing DOE missions. DOE cleanup contractor United Cleanup Oak Ridge (UCOR), an Amentum-led company, has been removing excess facilities across the reservation for the past 15 years.

title: SpaceNukes receives DARPA award to ground test kilopower reactor
summary: The Space Nuclear Power Corporation (SpaceNukes) was awarded an other transaction agreement from the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) to design, build, and conduct a nuclear ground test of a kilopower reactor in collaboration with Los Alamos National Laboratory, the company announced.

title: Entergy Arkansas’s Power to Care Golf Tournament raises $315,000 to support customers in need
summary: The 2026 Power to Care Golf Tournament brought together 54 teams, 48 sponsors and more than 70 volunteers to support Entergy Arkansas customers facing financial challenges and help them keep their power on by raising $315,000. Source

title: New Polling Reveals Majority Of Australians Support Nuclear Energy
summary: Almost two-thirds of Australians believe nuclear power should be part of the nation's energy future, as new polling reveals growing concerns about Australia's ability to meet its electricity needs. New YouGov research commissioned by lobby group Nuclear for Australia has found that 63% of Australians believe nuclear power should be considered, while 60% believe it will form part of Australia’s future energy mix. The findings come as both the demand for and cost of electricity grows, driven by AI, data centres and electrification, while the conflict in the Middle East contributes to uncertainty in global energy markets.

title: Integrated Repository For Slovenia’s Krško Plant And Test Reactor ‘Cheaper Than Standalone Site’
summary: Integrating a deep geologic repository for spent nuclear fuel from Slovenia’s Triga II research reactor into a site at the country’s Krško nuclear power plant would be cheaper than creating a standalone site, a study has shown. The study was carried out by Slovenia’s Agency for Radioactive Waste Management (Arao) and US-based Deep Isolation, which is developing nuclear waste disposal technologies in deep boreholes. The results showed that co-locating spent fuel from the Triga II reactor, which is at the Jožef Stefan Institute near the Slovenian capital of Ljubljana, would avoid duplicating costs over a standalone repository, which would require independent siting and licensing.
